title: CFrame
summary: Coordinate Frame: position AND orientation in one value. The right tool for placing, moving, and rotating parts and cameras. Built via CFrame.new, lookAt, Angles; composed with multiplication.

reference.signature: CFrame.new(x, y, z) / CFrame.lookAt(position, target) / CFrame.Angles(rx, ry, rz)

methods.name: CFrame.new
methods.description: Position-only, or position facing a point.

methods.name: CFrame.lookAt
methods.signature: CFrame.lookAt(at: Vector3, target: Vector3, up?: Vector3) --> CFrame
methods.description: Positioned at `at`, facing `target` — the clearest way to aim things.

methods.name: CFrame.Angles
methods.description: Rotation in RADIANS (wrap degrees with math.rad).

methods.name: ToWorldSpace / ToObjectSpace
methods.description: Convert between the frame's local space and world space.

details.heading: Multiplication = composition
details.body: `cfA * cfB` applies cfB relative to cfA's space: `part.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -5)` is 5 studs IN FRONT of the part, wherever it faces. Order matters: A*B ≠ B*A.

explanation.whatItIs: A full 'pose': where you are AND which way you face. Positions are points; CFrames are points with compass directions.
explanation.whyItExists: 3D objects need rotation as much as location. One composable value handles teleporting, aiming, orbiting, and attaching.
whenToUse: Offsets relative to facing: cf * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3) = '3 studs in front'
whenNotToUse: Physics-driven objects you want the engine to move
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
CFrame = position + 3 orientation axes
         ┌→ LookVector (forward, -Z)
    pos ─┼→ RightVector (+X)
         └→ UpVector (+Y)

cf * offset  = offset applied in cf's local space
A * B * C    = do C, then B, then A (right to left)
```
tips: lookAt for 'face that thing'; Angles for fixed tilts
Lerp alpha: clamp 0..1; framerate-independent alpha = 1 - math.exp(-rate * dt)
commonMistakes: Position-only changes when rotation matters — CFrame, not Vector3
Reversed multiplication order and mystery sideways offsets

examples.title: Facing and relative offsets
examples.code:
local part = workspace.Part

-- Face the nearest player:
local target = workspace.Dummy.Position
part.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(part.Position, target)

-- 5 studs in front of wherever it now faces:
part.CFrame = part.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -5)

-- Tilt 45 degrees around X:
part.CFrame = part.CFrame * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(45), 0, 0)

-- Spawn point: position + face a direction
local spawnCF = CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.new(0, 3, 0), Vector3.new(0, 3, -10))

examples.title: Smooth orbit
examples.code:
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local center = workspace.CenterPart
local orb = workspace.Orb

RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
    local angle = os.clock() % (2 * math.pi)
    local offset = Vector3.new(math.cos(angle), 0, math.sin(angle)) * 8
    orb.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(center.Position + offset + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0), center.Position)
end)
